paragraphs: Nittai of Tekoa brought ḥallah portions from Beitar; they did not accept them because it was outside the Land, Mishnah, end of Ḥallah. Jerusalem Talmud: since he was great and trustworthy, they refused so people would not learn to establish this as obligatory. The Mishnah there: ben Atitas—so Arukh; some read Antoninos, while Temurah 21a reads Antigonos—brought firstborn animals from Babylonia, and they refused them. Yosef the priest brought first-fruits of wine and oil, and they refused; Ariston brought his first-fruits from Apamya, and they accepted. All were pious and renowned; hence I mentioned them.
